title: Anaemia in Pregnancy: Screening and Treatment

evidenceAudit.scope: Pregnant or postnatal woman with anaemia: haemoglobin and ferritin thresholds, oral iron, intravenous iron, monitoring and intrapartum precautions, using the BNSSG guideline based on the British Society for Haematology 2019 guideline. Medicine-pathway restructure on 2026-10-18: medicines regrouped into branches, steps and give-all vs choose-one options; no dose, source or clinical claim was re-checked.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-18.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.

Medicine list restructured into a branched decision pathway on 2026-10-18. Doses, routes, adjustments, monitoring, contraindications and sources are unchanged from authoring-standard-2026-10-18-tier3b-v1-live.
unverifiedSections: Only one local NHS guideline (BNSSG version 3, valid to March 2025, so it may be out of date) was opened; the British Society for Haematology guideline itself and NICE antenatal care guidance were not opened.
The document gives no vitamin B12 or folate treatment doses.
The document does not specify a 2-week haemoglobin response check; it reassesses haemoglobin and ferritin 4 weeks after the dose.
Symptoms and signs are general clinical features and are not listed in the extracts opened.
No Saudi Ministry of Health guideline was opened.
Source pages were read through automated page extraction rather than page-by-page in the original documents, so each figure should be spot-checked against the source during clinical review.
The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.

Medicine pathway: branch entry criteria, preferred options and “use when” conditions were assigned from this topic's own indications and management steps. Confirm each against the cited guideline before clinical use.

pathophysiology.summary: Haemoglobin thresholds for anaemia differ by trimester and postpartum. Ferritin below 30 mcg/L indicates significant iron depletion regardless of haemoglobin. Other causes include vitamin B12 and folate deficiency. Intravenous iron carries a hypersensitivity risk and needs anaphylaxis equipment available.
keyMechanisms: Haemoglobin thresholds for anaemia differ by trimester and postpartum.

Other causes include vitamin B12 and folate deficiency.

clinicalManagement.title: Diagnose
actions: Measure haemoglobin and ferritin; apply WHO thresholds.

clinicalManagement.title: Oral iron
actions: Give 40 to 80 mg elemental iron a day; once daily for risk factors, alternate days (Monday, Wednesday, Friday) for others or if daily doses are difficult.
Take about 1 hour before meals with a vitamin C source.

clinicalManagement.title: Intravenous iron if needed
actions: For intolerance or non-response to oral iron, or late pregnancy and postnatal criteria above.
Ferinject: maximum single dose 20 mg/kg up to 1,000 mg per visit; no more than 1,000 mg per week.

clinicalManagement.title: Recheck
actions: Reassess haemoglobin and ferritin 4 weeks after the dose.

clinicalManagement.title: Intrapartum precautions
actions: Haemoglobin below 100 g/L: alert obstetric and anaesthetic teams, offer active third-stage management and consider intravenous access (required if below 90 g/L).

regimens.indication: Iron deficiency anaemia in pregnancy and postpartum (first line)
regimens.genericName: Oral iron (for example Pregaday: ferrous fumarate 100 mg elemental iron with folic acid 350 mcg)
regimens.dose: 40 to 80 mg elemental iron per day (Pregaday one tablet contains 100 mg elemental iron)
regimens.frequency: Once daily if risk factors; alternate days (Monday, Wednesday, Friday) for others
regimens.duration: Postnatal at least 6 weeks; after intravenous iron start once-daily oral iron 5 days after the last infusion for 3 months
adjustments: Elemental iron per tablet: ferrous sulphate 200 mg = 65 mg; ferrous gluconate 300 mg = 35 mg; ferrous fumarate 322 mg = 100 mg.
Take about 1 hour before meals with vitamin C.
monitoring: Haemoglobin and ferritin 4 weeks after starting; no repeat ferritin before 4 weeks.
contraindications: Contraindications are not listed in the extract opened; check product information.

regimens.sourceEdition: BNSSG Anaemia Antenatal and Post Natal v3, pp. 2 to 3

regimens.indication: Iron deficiency anaemia not responding to or intolerant of oral iron
regimens.patientGroup: Pregnant from second trimester, and postnatal women
regimens.dose: Maximum single dose 20 mg/kg, up to 1,000 mg per visit; total by haemoglobin and weight: haemoglobin below 100 g/L 1,500 mg (35 to 70 kg) or 2,000 mg (70 kg or more); 100 to below 140 g/L 1,000 mg or 1,500 mg
regimens.frequency: Single dose per visit; remainder after 1 week, no more than 1,000 mg per week
adjustments: Weight below 35 kg: do not exceed 500 mg.
monitoring: Baseline and post-infusion observations; observe about 15 minutes; haemoglobin and ferritin 4 weeks after total dose (after the second dose if over 1,000 mg).
contraindications: First trimester; anaemia not due to iron deficiency; previous hypersensitivity to intravenous iron; iron overload; infusion within 7 days; acute infection; abnormal liver function.
Caution in thalassaemia, sickle cell disease, asthma, eczema or atopic allergy.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Haemoglobin below 110 g/L first trimester; below 105 g/L second and third trimester; below 100 g/L postpartum.
Second trimester onward for iron deficiency anaemia with intolerance or non-response to oral iron; consider after 34 weeks with haemoglobin below 105 g/L; postnatal haemoglobin below 90 g/L.

teaching.scope: Pregnant or postnatal woman with anaemia: haemoglobin and ferritin thresholds, oral iron, intravenous iron, monitoring and intrapartum precautions, using the BNSSG guideline based on the British Society for Haematology 2019 guideline.
learningObjectives: Use trimester-specific haemoglobin thresholds and ferritin below 30 mcg/L.
Use oral iron first and intravenous iron for failure or late presentation.
pitfalls: Giving intravenous iron in acute infection.
keyPoints: Intravenous iron is not given in the first trimester.

dischargeCriteria: Haemoglobin improved and plan for iron status check by primary care at the end of treatment.
